P1_index_answers_instead_of_narrowing._note: The design's load-bearing distinction: the index narrows the CANDIDATES, the base class's own predicate still decides. Trusting the index outright makes every cache-unjudgeable path — always a candidate — answer every query, and the fixture's earliest-sorting one then wins both the anchor lookup and the status lookup. Predicted C1/C3/C4/C5/C9; MEASURED C1/C3/C4/C6/C7. C5 and C9 do not execute this code at all (the conflict diagnostic comes from `PropertyNameValidator`'s own walk, C9 calls `ShapeLoader` directly), while C6 goes red because the bogus anchor fails the isDefinedBy range guard and C7 because it asserts the uid lookup returns THAT file, not the first candidate (integration-test-revert-verify §A44).

P2_unjudgeable_paths_not_candidates._note: Same invariant as the cache-side M3, on the consuming side: a uid only a converter-SKIPPED file carries must still resolve.
